lines.text: Today you will train your mouth like a sports star trains their muscles, so every word comes out clear.
For v, gently bite your bottom lip with your top teeth and buzz, like van and very.
For w, make your lips round like a little O, then open them, like water and window.
Your teeth do not touch your lip for w.
Put the tip of your tongue lightly between your teeth and blow.
Think, three and thank you blow air quietly.
This, that and mother add a buzz.
The -ed at the end of past words has three sounds.
Walked and jumped end like t.
Played and cleaned end like d.
Say important words a little louder and longer.
Pause for a breath at every comma and full stop.
Pauses help your listener understand you.
Let us warm up our mouths. For the v sound, top teeth touch the bottom lip. Van, very, violin.
For the w sound, make round lips and open them. Wet, window, water.
Now try the pairs slowly. Vest, west. Vet, wet. Can you hear the difference?
Listen to the endings. I walked to the park. Walked ends with a quick t sound.
I played with my friend. Played ends with a soft d sound.
We wanted ice cream. Wanted has an extra beat at the end. Want, ed.
Only words ending in a t or d sound, like want and need, get that extra beat.
Listen to how this reader uses pauses and stress.
Every Wednesday, my brother and I visit the vegetable market.
We buy fresh, green beans and very sweet watermelons.
Then we walk home, tired but happy. Notice the short breath at every comma.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
